headline: Earnings jump as Cadence integration wraps and fees grow
summary_short: Huntington's Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $0.33 rose $0.08 q/q (down $0.01 y/y) as net income jumped 39% q/q to $727 million, aided by the completed Cadence systems conversion and broad growth in net interest and fee income.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 9% q/q, 40% y/y to $2.05B on Cadence/Veritex-driven loan growth (+9% q/q, +42% y/y); NIM slipped 3bp q/q to 3.21% but is up 10bp y/y. Noninterest income grew 15% q/q, 67% y/y to $785M, led by capital markets/advisory, mortgage banking, and payments fees. Reported EPS of $0.33 absorbed $152M of acquisition-related Notable Items (vs $263M in Q1); adjusted EPS was $0.39, up $0.02 q/q. NPAs rose to 0.85% of loans (+13bp q/q); net charge-offs held near 0.25%. CET1 fell to 10.0% from 10.2% on higher risk-weighted assets and buybacks; tangible book value per share rose 1% to $9.65. No quantified forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites disciplined execution, strong legacy-franchise growth, early Cadence revenue synergies, and completion of the Cadence systems conversion as drivers of the quarter.

Q/q growth driven by a 9% rise in net interest income (higher average earning assets/loans, partly Cadence) and 15% growth in noninterest income led by capital markets, mortgage banking, and payments fees.
Higher net interest and noninterest income drove the q/q increase, partly offset by $152M of acquisition-related Notable Items versus $263M in Q1.
Tracks the net income increase; adjusted EPS excluding Notable Items was $0.39, up $0.02 q/q, versus $0.33 reported.
3bp q/q decline reflected a modest increase in overall funding costs, partially offsetting higher earning-asset yields.
Decline driven by higher risk-weighted assets and the impact of share repurchases, partly offset by current-period earnings net of dividends.
Increase driven by higher commercial & industrial, residential mortgage, and commercial real estate nonaccruals, including some acquired via Cadence and Veritex.

Not separately explained; the release attributes the related TCE/tangible-assets ratio increase to retained earnings net of dividends and lower tangible assets, partly offset by buybacks and lower AOCI.
